Duśśāsana
(‘One who is difficult to control’)
------------------------------------------
Born as the second son of धृतराष्ट्र and गान्धारी, दुश्शासन was next to दुर्योधन in age but worse in vulgarity and vileness. He laid the foundation for the कुरुक्षेत्र war by dragging the princess द्रौपदी to the open court and dis-honouring her, after the first game of dice.
He was defeated in his combats with the heroes in the Pāṇḍava army several times. अर्जुन, अभिमन्यु and सात्यकि had that privilege. He was finally killed in his combat with भीम.

Duṣyanta
------------------------------------------
One of the famous couples in Hindu म्य्थोलोग्य् who have attracted the attention of writers in Sanskrit literature is दुष्यन्त and शकुन्तला.
Duṣyanta was the son of Ilila and a scion of the famous चन्द्र Vaṁśa. His first wife was Lākṣi or लक्षणा.
When दुष्यन्त went to the forest for hunting, he chanced to meet शकुन्तला (the daughter of Menakā from the sage विश्वामित्र) in the hermitage of the sage कण्व. They fell in love with each other and married by the गान्धर्व rite. दुष्यन्त left, promising to come again and take her to his place. He did not turn up even after five years. Hence the sage कण्व, the foster-ड़थेर् of शकुन्तला, took her, along with her child Sarvadamana-भरत, to the king. Due to a curse the king had forgotten the whole affair and hence refused to accept शकुन्तला. However there was an ‘ākāśa vāṇī’ (voice from the void) confirming शकुन्तला’s statement thereby making the king accept her.
Bharata succeeded him to the throne. It was his extraordinary greatness that made this country (India) go by his name as ‘Bharatakhaṇḍa’ or ‘Bharatavarṣa’
Kālidāsa’s famous work Abhijñāna-Śākuntalam is based on this story of दुष्यन्त.
See also ŚAKUNTALĀ.
